verdict: AppLovin turned $1.84B of revenue — up 59% — into $1.21B of net profit, a 65% margin, as its AXON ad platform kept compounding.

segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show. AppLovin sold its own apps business in 2025, so this platform is the whole company.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the AXON ad platform — up 67% YoY as AppLovin pours money into AI-driven ad targeting.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to advertisers and app publishers — roughly flat YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — down 15% YoY as AppLovin streamlined after selling its apps business.

takeaways.title: Growth stayed hot
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 59% to $1.84B as advertisers kept shifting budgets to AXON — a year ago the same platform did $1.16B in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Two-thirds kept as profit
takeaways.text: Net income of $1.21B is 65% of revenue — an almost unheard-of margin for an ad business, because software costs almost nothing extra to deliver.

takeaways.title: Cash in, buybacks out
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $1.29B in a single quarter, and AppLovin spent about $1.0B buying back its own shares.

otherDetail: Other income of $43M (mostly investment and foreign-exchange gains), partly offset by $51M of interest expense on AppLovin's debt.
footerNote: AppLovin reports as a single segment. Its former apps business was sold in 2025 and appears as discontinued operations in earlier periods; there were none this quarter.
